mainTopic: Preventing חמץ: wet wheat, flour in a pot or in sharp foods, and the משנה about חרוסת, mustard, the קרבן פסח, and a baker's water.
overview: The amud opens at the end of a story about how carefully wheat was kept dry for מצה. Next, a boat of wheat sinks in a river, and רבא first allows the wet wheat to be sold to גוים. רבה בר לוואי challenges him with a ברייתא about a garment with hidden כלאים, since a גוי might resell it to a Jew. רבא changes his ruling: sell the wheat to Jews in small amounts, so it is all eaten before פסח. A ברייתא then discusses stirring flour into a pot on פסח with vinegar. רב חסדא links the lenient view to רבי יהודה, while עולא forbids every method. The גמרא also tells of roasted grain stirred into pots, with two versions of רבא's view. A new משנה forbids flour in חרוסת or mustard, cooking the קרבן פסח in liquids, and keeping a baker's used water. The גמרא limits the argument to mustard and rules like the חכמים, and רב נחמן בר יצחק begins a question that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: His mother guarded his wheat in troughs
steps.stepSummary: This line finishes the story about מר בריה דרבינא. His mother kept his wheat in troughs so it would stay dry for מצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: His mother would gather the wheat for him in troughs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a story that began on the previous amud. It tells us how carefully the mother of מר בריה דרבינא protected his wheat from getting wet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She kept the wheat in troughs so no water could reach it. Wet wheat could become חמץ. This shows a very high level of guarding for מצה, called שימור, starting long before פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: would gather or collect for him

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse אַרְבֵי (troughs) here with אַרְבָּא (a boat) in the next line. The two words look alike but mean different things.

phrases.english: His mother would gather [the wheat] for him in troughs.
phrases.notes: This finishes the story about מר בריה דרבינא from the previous section.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a story that started in the text on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Extra care was taken to keep wheat for מצה completely dry, by storing it in troughs.

steps.title: רבא allows selling wheat from a sunken boat to gentiles
steps.stepSummary: A boat carrying wheat sank in the river חישתא. רבא allowed the owners to sell the wet wheat to גוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain boat of wheat that sank in the river חישתא. רבא allowed it to be sold to גוים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story about wheat that became soaked in water. רבא gives a ruling: the owners may sell it to גוים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wheat soaked in water may become חמץ, so a Jew should not keep it for פסח. רבא found a way out: sell it to a גוי before פסח. This ruling is what the next steps will challenge.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of the sugya asks whether selling something forbidden to a גוי is safe. The worry is that the item could end up back in Jewish hands.

phrases.english: A certain boat of wheat
that sank in the Ḥishta [river].
Rava permitted [them] to sell it to gentiles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new case that is also about wet wheat and the risk of חמץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wheat that sank and got soaked may be sold to גוים.

steps.title: רבה בר לוואי quotes a ברייתא about a garment with lost כלאים
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר לוואי challenges רבא by quoting a ברייתא. A garment with a hidden thread of כלאים may not be sold to a גוי or made into a donkey's saddlecloth. It may, however, be used as burial shrouds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר לוואי challenged רבא from a ברייתא: A garment in which a thread of כלאים got lost may not be sold to a גוי. It also may not be made into a saddlecloth for a donkey. But it may be made into shrouds for a dead person.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר לוואי brings a ברייתא to argue against רבא. This step only quotes the source. The next step explains why the source is a problem for רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The garment has a thread of the wrong material sewn into it, and no one can find it. The ברייתא forbids selling it to a גוי and even using it for a donkey, because someone might later wear it. Shrouds are allowed, since no one will take cloth back from a dead body.

keyTerms.meaning: he raised an objection against him from a source
a forbidden mix of wool and linen (שעטנז)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the cases. The ברייתא is about clothing, not wheat. Its connection to רבא's case only becomes clear in the next step.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Levai raised an objection to Rava:
A garment in which diverse kinds were lost
one may not sell it to a gentile,
and one may not make it into a saddlecloth for a donkey.
But one may make it into shrouds for a dead person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to challenge רבא's ruling from Step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's permission to sell the soaked wheat to גוים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא forbids selling a hidden forbidden item to a גוי. This suggests the same should be true for the wheat.

steps.title: The reason: the gentile may resell it to a Jew
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא matters. The ban on selling to a גוי seems to come from the fear that he will resell it to a Jew. The same fear should apply to the wheat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why may it not be sold to a גוי? Is it not because he might turn around and sell it to a Jew?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge by giving the reason behind the ברייתא's rule. Once we see that reason, it clearly works against רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one can see the כלאים in the garment, so a Jew could buy it from the גוי without knowing. In the same way, no one can tell that the wheat was soaked. So a גוי might resell the wheat to a Jew, who would then eat חמץ on פסח. That makes רבא's ruling look wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: that he will turn around and resell

steps.whatToRemember: The challenge to רבא depends on one shared point: the problem is hidden in both cases. A גוי might pass the item back to an unknowing Jew.

phrases.english: To a gentile, what is the reason [one may] not [sell it]?
Is it not because he will turn around and sell it to a Jew?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the reasoning out of the ברייתא from Step 3 so it can be used against רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling allowing the sale of the soaked wheat to גוים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a hidden problem bans selling to a גוי because he may resell to a Jew, then the soaked wheat should also be banned. Its problem is just as hidden.

steps.title: רבא changes his ruling: sell the wheat to Jews in small amounts
steps.stepSummary: After the challenge from רבה בר לוואי, רבא withdraws his first ruling. He now says the wet wheat should be sold to Jews one קב at a time, so it is used up before פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא then changed his mind and said: Let them sell the wheat one קב at a time to Jews, so that it will be finished before פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא accepts the challenge and gives a new ruling. The wheat should not go to גוים at all. Instead, it should be sold to Jews in small amounts that will be eaten before פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that a גוי might resell the wheat to a Jew who would keep it until פסח. If each Jew buys only a small amount, he will finish it quickly, long before פסח arrives. The danger is removed by the way the wheat is sold, not by who it is sold to.

keyTerms.meaning: A קב, a small dry measure

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's final ruling: wet wheat should be sold in small amounts to Jews, so that no one is left holding it when פסח comes.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a practical way to handle food that may become חמץ. Instead of banning the sale, you sell it in a way that guarantees it will be finished in time.

phrases.english: Rava reconsidered and said:
phrases.notes: הדר signals that רבא is withdrawing his earlier ruling.

phrases.english: Let them sell it one kav at a time to Jews,
phrases.notes: Small amounts, each to a different buyer.

phrases.english: so that it will be used up before Passover.
phrases.notes: Each buyer finishes his small share quickly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא answers the challenge from steps 3-4 by changing his ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retraction and revised ruling: the original permission is withdrawn and replaced with a safer method of sale.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Selling the wet wheat to גוים is allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Sell the wheat in small amounts to Jews so that it is all eaten before פסח.

steps.title: ברייתא: stirring flour into a pot on פסח
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that one may not stir flour into a pot on פסח. One who wants to may add the flour first and then vinegar. A second view, called יש אומרים, allows adding vinegar first and then the flour.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: One may not stir flour into a pot on Passover. One who wants to stir should put in the flour and afterward put in the vinegar. And some say: He may even put in the vinegar first and afterward put in the flour.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic. It quotes a ברייתא about adding flour to a cooking pot on פסח, and how vinegar can prevent the flour from becoming חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Flour mixed with water can become חמץ, so stirring it into a pot is forbidden. The first view allows it only if vinegar is added after the flour. The יש אומרים go further: vinegar works even when it is in the pot before the flour, so its power to prevent leavening is very strong.

keyTerms.meaning: Stirring or crumbling flour into food

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One may not stir flour into a pot on Passover.
phrases.notes: The flour was added to soak up the foam in the pot.

phrases.english: And one who wishes to stir in flour —
puts in the flour
and afterward puts in the vinegar.
phrases.notes: The vinegar keeps the flour from becoming חמץ.

phrases.english: And some say:
he may even put in the vinegar first
and afterward put in the flour.
phrases.notes: The vinegar still works even though the flour came second.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. It moves from the wet-wheat story to the use of flour in cooking on פסח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Stirring flour into a pot on פסח is forbidden unless vinegar is added after the flour. According to the יש אומרים, adding vinegar before the flour is also allowed.

steps.title: Who is the unnamed 'some say' opinion?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds the view of the יש אומרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the one called 'some say'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question: who is behind the unnamed opinion in the ברייתא? This sets up the next step, where רב חסדא gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unnamed opinions are often matched to a known תנא. Finding the source tells us what larger idea this view is built on.

phrases.english: Who is 'some say'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the identity of the second opinion in the ברייתא of step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא behind the יש אומרים opinion.

steps.title: רב חסדא: it is רבי יהודה, who treats vinegar as strong as boiling
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the יש אומרים is רבי יהודה. He proves this from a משנה about שבת. There, רבי יהודה forbids adding spices to a removed pot only when it contains vinegar or brine, because he treats them as if they were still boiling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It is רבי יהודה. As we learned in a משנה: A stew pot or a pot that one took off the fire while boiling — one may not put spices into them, but one may put spices into a bowl or a serving plate. רבי יהודה says: One may put spices into anything, except a dish that has vinegar or brine in it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question: the יש אומרים is רבי יהודה. He supports this with a משנה from the laws of cooking on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a pot taken off the fire is no longer treated as cooking once its food is moved to another dish. רבי יהודה says that vinegar or brine gives food a power like boiling heat. If vinegar is that strong, it can also stop flour from becoming חמץ even when the flour is added after the vinegar.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה

steps.whatToRemember: The יש אומרים is רבי יהודה. In his view, vinegar acts like boiling heat, so it prevents flour from becoming חמץ no matter which is added first.
steps.confusionAlert: The משנה quoted here is about cooking on שבת, not about פסח. רב חסדא brings it only to show how strong vinegar is in רבי יהודה's view.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the גמרא connects two separate areas of law, שבת cooking and חמץ, through one shared idea: how strong vinegar is.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
It is Rabbi Yehuda,
as we learned in a Mishnah:
A stew pot or a pot that one took off the fire while boiling —
one may not put spices into them,
phrases.notes: On שבת, because the boiling heat would cook the spices.

phrases.english: but one may put them into a bowl
or into a serving plate.
phrases.notes: Food moved into a second dish is no longer treated as cooking.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
one may put spices into anything,

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ מִדָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ חוֹמֶץ וָצִיר.
phrases.english: except a dish that has vinegar or brine in it.
phrases.notes: Vinegar or brine makes the food act as if it were still boiling.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7 by naming רבי יהודה and proving it from a משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The יש אומרים is רבי יהודה, who treats vinegar as having the strength of boiling heat.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה would hold vinegar prevents leavening even when it is added before the flour.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about adding spices on שבת, where רבי יהודה treats a dish with vinegar or brine as if it were still boiling.

steps.title: Why not say the second view is רבי יוסי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the יש אומרים could follow רבי יוסי, who holds that vinegar stops grain from becoming חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say the יש אומרים follows רבי יוסי. We learned in a משנה that רבי יוסי says: soak the grains in vinegar, and the vinegar makes them shrink so they do not become חמץ.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא said the יש אומרים is רבי יהודה. Now the גמרא asks why not link it to רבי יוסי instead, since he clearly says vinegar prevents חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The יש אומרים allows putting vinegar in first and the flour after. רבי יוסי holds that vinegar makes grain shrink so it cannot become חמץ. So the יש אומרים seems to fit him perfectly, and we would not need רב חסדא's indirect proof from a שבת law.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us establish it (attribute it to a certain view)
Makes them shrink or contract, so they do not become חמץ

phrases.english: But let us establish it according to Rabbi Yosei,
phrases.notes: 'It' refers to the view of the יש אומרים from the ברייתא.

phrases.english: (as we learned in a Mishnah) Rabbi Yosei says:
One soaks them in vinegar,
phrases.notes: Speaking of grains that got wet.

phrases.english: and the vinegar makes them contract!
phrases.notes: So they cannot become חמץ.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's attribution of the יש אומרים to רבי יהודה by offering a more direct source.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that the יש אומרים is רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי says plainly that vinegar prevents חמץ, so the יש אומרים (vinegar first) fits him more directly.

steps.title: רבי יוסי only relies on pure vinegar
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי's rule works only with pure vinegar, not vinegar mixed into a pot of food.
steps.simpleTranslation: When we taught רבי יוסי's view, that is only where the vinegar is pure and whole. But when it is part of a mixture, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why the יש אומרים cannot simply be רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's vinegar works because it is strong and undiluted. In a pot, the vinegar is mixed with water and other food, so it is much weaker. רבי יוסי never said weak, mixed vinegar can stop חמץ, so the יש אומרים needs רבי יהודה's idea instead.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply only to... (a limiting phrase)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי is not saying vinegar stops working completely. He only relies on it when it is pure. Inside a cooking pot it is diluted, so his rule does not reach that case.

phrases.english: When we heard Rabbi Yosei's view,
that applies only where the vinegar is in its pure form,
but by means of a mixture, no.
phrases.notes: Vinegar diluted in a pot is too weak for רבי יוסי's rule.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by narrowing רבי יוסי's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the cited source (pure vs. mixed vinegar).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי's vinegar rule covers any use of vinegar, including in a pot.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי only relies on pure vinegar. The יש אומרים rests on רבי יהודה's view that vinegar in a pot counts as if still boiling.

steps.title: עולא forbids both methods
steps.stepSummary: עולא rules that flour in a pot is forbidden either way, because one should keep far from anything that could lead to a sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: both this way and that way are forbidden. As people say to a נזיר: 'Go around, go around, and do not come near the vineyard.'
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives his own ruling: no flour may go into the pot on פסח, whichever comes first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both earlier views tried to find a safe order of vinegar and flour. עולא says we should not take any risk at all with חמץ. Like a נזיר who should avoid even walking near a vineyard, a person should stay far from situations that might lead to real חמץ.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this and that (both cases equally)
A נזיר, who may not have wine or grapes
Go around, go around (keep your distance)

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of 'staying away from the vineyard' is a well-known principle for adding protective distance around serious prohibitions.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
Both this and that are forbidden,
phrases.notes: Vinegar first or flour first.

phrases.english: because of the saying: 'Go, go, we say to the nazirite,
go around, go around, do not come near the vineyard.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a stricter third view on the ברייתא's case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Putting flour into a pot on פסח is forbidden whether vinegar is added first or after, as a protective distance from חמץ.

steps.title: רב פפי lets the cooks use roasted grain
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי allowed the cooks of the ריש גלותא to stir roasted grain into a pot on פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפי permitted the cooks of the house of the ריש גלותא to stir roasted grain into a pot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a real practice, which sets up רבא's reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Roasted grain has already been heated, so it can no longer become חמץ. That is why רב פפי allowed it even though plain flour in a pot is a problem. The cooks used it to settle the foam in the pot.

keyTerms.meaning: The Exilarch, head of the Jewish community in Bavel
Roasted grain, which can no longer become חמץ

phrases.english: Rav Pappi permitted
the cooks of the Exilarch's household
to stir roasted grain into a pot.
phrases.notes: Roasted grain cannot become חמץ.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פַּפִּי שָׁרֵי לֵיהּ לְבוּרְדִּיקִי דְּבֵי רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from flour to a related case of roasted grain in a pot.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Roasted grain may be stirred into a pot on פסח.

steps.title: רבא objects: servants will not be careful
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects to allowing this where servants cook, since they may use regular flour instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Would anyone permit such a thing in a place where servants are found?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רב פפי's permission.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not argue that roasted grain is חמץ. His worry is that servants will not tell the difference and will put plain flour into the pot. That would lead to real חמץ on פסח.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Is there anyone who permits such a thing
in a place where servants are found?
phrases.notes: They may use raw flour instead.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אִיכָּא דְּשָׁרֵי כִּי הַאי מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Objects to רב פפי's permission.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפי's permission for the ריש גלותא's cooks.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Careless servants may use plain flour instead of roasted grain, leading to real חמץ.

steps.title: Another version: רבא did it himself
steps.stepSummary: Another version reports that רבא himself stirred roasted grain into his own pot.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רבא himself stirred roasted grain into a pot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the story, in which רבא himself followed the lenient practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a different tradition about רבא, introduced with איכא דאמרי. In step 13, רבא objected to the practice, at least where servants are around. In this version, he not only allows roasted grain but uses it in his own pot.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say (an alternate version of the report)

steps.whatToRemember: Flour in a pot on פסח: the יש אומרים (based on רבי יהודה) allows vinegar first, and עולא forbids every method. Roasted grain is different, since it cannot become חמץ. רבא only worried about careless servants, and in one version he used it himself.

phrases.english: Some say:

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא גּוּפָא מָחֵי לֵהּ קִידְרָא בַּחֲסִיסֵי.
phrases.english: Rava himself would stir roasted grain into a pot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternate tradition about רבא's own practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Roasted grain in a pot is permitted, and רבא himself did this.

steps.title: No flour in חרוסת or mustard
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says not to put flour into חרוסת or mustard. If someone did, the חכמים say to eat it immediately, and רבי מאיר forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may not put flour into חרוסת or into mustard. If he did put it in, it should be eaten immediately. רבי מאיר forbids it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. Its first ruling says not to mix flour into sharp foods like חרוסת or mustard on פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that flour sitting in these moist foods could turn into חמץ. The חכמים think it takes time to leaven, so eating it right away is safe. רבי מאיר is afraid it could become חמץ right away, so he forbids it completely.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. This marks the start of the משנה text.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
One may not put flour
into charoses or into mustard.
phrases.notes: People added flour to tone down the sharp taste.

phrases.english: And if he did put it in, it should be eaten immediately,
phrases.notes: This means before it has time to become חמץ.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Meir forbids it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין נוֹתְנִין קֶמַח לְתוֹךְ חֲרוֹסֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The earlier discussion of flour in a pot is over. A new משנה starts here.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not put flour into חרוסת or mustard at the start. If it was done, the חכמים say eat it right away. רבי מאיר forbids it.

steps.title: The קרבן פסח may not be cooked in liquids
steps.stepSummary: The קרבן פסח may not be cooked in liquids or fruit juices. It may be basted with them and dipped into them.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not cook the קרבן פסח in liquids or in fruit juices. But one may baste it with them and dip it into them.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the משנה's second ruling. It is about how the קרבן פסח must be prepared.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה requires the פסח to be roasted, so cooking it in any liquid is not allowed. Basting it while it roasts, or dipping it while eating, does not turn roasting into cooking. So those are permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: the קרבן פסח, the Passover lamb
Liquids, such as wine, oil, or water

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that roasting, the only way the פסח may be prepared, is not ruined by adding liquid from the outside.

phrases.english: One may not cook the Pesach offering
not in liquids and not in fruit juices,
phrases.notes: The תורה commands that it be roasted only.

phrases.english: but one may baste it and dip it in them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין מְבַשְּׁלִין אֶת הַפֶּסַח לֹא בְּמַשְׁקִין וְלֹא בְּמֵי פֵירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the next ruling in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסח may not be cooked in liquids or fruit juices. Basting and dipping are allowed.

steps.title: A baker's used water must be poured out
steps.stepSummary: Water that a baker used must be poured out, because it causes leavening.
steps.simpleTranslation: The water a baker uses must be poured out, because it causes leavening.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the משנה's third ruling. A baker's used water must be thrown away on פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A baker uses water to cool his hands or rinse his utensils, so it holds bits of flour and dough. That water can become חמץ and can make other things leaven. So it must be poured out.

phrases.english: The water used by a baker
phrases.notes: For example, water used to cool his hands or wash his dishes.

phrases.english: must be poured out, because it causes leavening.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the last ruling in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A baker's used water must be poured out because it causes leavening.

steps.title: The argument is only about mustard
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא says the חכמים and רבי מאיר argue only about mustard. With חרוסת, everyone agrees the mixture must be burned immediately.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב כהנא said: The argument is about flour put into mustard. But if it was put into חרוסת, everyone agrees it must be burned immediately.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. רב כהנא explains that the משנה's argument does not cover both foods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mustard is so sharp that it slows the flour from leavening. So the חכמים allow eating it right away, while רבי מאיר still forbids it. חרוסת is milder, so the flour leavens quickly, and even the חכמים agree the mixture is already חמץ and must be burned.

keyTerms.meaning: The גמרא, the Talmud's discussion of the משנה
An אמורא, a sage of the גמרא period

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two uses of מיד. In the משנה, יאכל מיד means 'eat it immediately,' and that is allowed. Here, ישרף מיד means 'burn it immediately,' because it is already חמץ. Also note: the milder חרוסת leavens faster, not the sharper mustard.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר and the חכמים argue only about mustard. Flour in חרוסת must be burned according to everyone.

phrases.english: Gemara:
Rav Kahana said:
The argument is about flour put into mustard,
phrases.notes: Mustard's sharpness slows down leavening.

phrases.english: but if it was put into charoses,
everyone agrees it must be burned immediately.
phrases.notes: It leavens quickly, so it is already חמץ.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא מַחֲלוֹקֶת לְתוֹךְ הַחַרְדָּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This explains the first ruling of the משנה (step 15). It narrows the argument there to mustard only.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument applies only to mustard. Flour in חרוסת must be burned immediately according to everyone.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב כהנא: the argument is only about mustard
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says flour in חרוסת must be burned immediately, with no argument. רבי מאיר and the חכמים argue only about mustard. This matches רב כהנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a ברייתא also teaches this: We do not put flour into חרוסת, and if someone did, it must be burned immediately. If flour was put into mustard, רבי מאיר says it must be burned immediately, and the חכמים say it must be eaten immediately.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up what רב כהנא just said in step 18.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the rule for חרוסת has no name attached. So everyone agrees it must be burned. The argument is placed only on mustard, which is exactly how רב כהנא explained the משנה. This makes רב כהנא's reading the clear one: חרוסת is more dangerous, and the only debate is about mustard.

keyTerms.meaning: And a ברייתא also teaches this (a support formula)
A dip made of fruit and vinegar or wine
It must be eaten immediately (before it can become חמץ)

steps.whyThisMatters: It confirms that flour in חרוסת is treated more strictly than flour in mustard. Everyone agrees the חרוסת mixture is burned.

phrases.english: And it was also taught in a baraita like this:
phrases.notes: Formula that brings a supporting source

phrases.english: One may not put flour into the charoset,
and if he did put it in, it must be burned immediately.
phrases.notes: No name attached, so this is agreed by all

phrases.english: If it was put into mustard,
Rabbi Meir says: it must be burned immediately,
and the Sages say: it must be eaten immediately.
phrases.notes: Eat it quickly, before it has time to leaven

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב כהנא's statement in step 18
steps.raayaObject: רב כהנא's claim that the argument is only about mustard, and that חרוסת is burned according to everyone
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that puts the חרוסת rule without any argument and puts the argument only on mustard

steps.title: שמואל rules that the הלכה follows the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: Through a chain of names, שמואל rules that the הלכה follows the חכמים in the mustard case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא the son of רב יהודה said in the name of רב נחמן, who said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה follows the words of the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a practical ruling: in the argument between רבי מאיר and the חכמים, we follow the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling is passed down through three people: שמואל, then רב נחמן, then רב הונא בריה דרב יהודה. It decides the mustard argument in favor of the more lenient view of the חכמים. The ruling does not say which version of the חכמים' words it means, and that gap sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows the words of the חכמים

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume it is already clear what 'the חכמים' ruled. The very next line asks exactly that, because the חכמים' view appears in two different forms (the משנה and the ברייתא).

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehuda, said
that Rav Nachman said that Shmuel said:
phrases.notes: A chain of transmission

phrases.english: The halacha is like the words of the Sages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the argument that the ברייתא in step 19 just showed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows the חכמים: flour in mustard is eaten immediately rather than burned.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק turns to question רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק begins to address רב הונא בריה דרב יהודה about the ruling just given. His actual question comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said to רב הונא the son of רב יהודה:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is preparing a question about which version of the חכמים' ruling שמואל meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line only tells us who is speaking and to whom. It aims the question straight at the person who reported שמואל's ruling, so we expect a request to clarify what that ruling means.

keyTerms.meaning: He said to him (introduces a reply or question to a specific person)
An אמורא who questions the ruling just reported

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said to him,
to Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehuda:
phrases.notes: The question itself continues on the next amud

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק לְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the ruling in step 20
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly the ruling 'like the חכמים' means (the question itself continues on the next amud)
